Hi Priya / Jordan / Sofia,

Quick technical note on KMS/key custody and telemetry pseudonymization:

- Hosted (Redwood API): Customer data-at-rest is encrypted with keys managed by Redwood KMS. For customers requiring dedicated key custody we offer a Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) option via a supported cloud KMS provider; logs of key usage are retained for 90 days by default and can be extended under contract. The attached attestation PDF contains the lifecycle table (create -> rotate -> retire -> destroy) and a short description of safeguards (HSM-backed, access gating, audit logs).

- Subprocessor handling: Only a subset of subprocessors handle decrypted PII (examples: on-prem data extractors, localization teams under NDA). For those, we require contract clauses that limit cross-border transfers and require prior notice + written consent. We maintain an internal exports registry and will provide country-by-function mapping in the bundle.

- Telemetry: We pseudonymize identifiers before sending to analytics subprocessors. Pseudonymization uses salted hashing and tokenization; mapping tables for re-identification are stored in a separate, access-controlled vault. We can provide a short technical note describing the pseudonymization and re-identification controls if your team needs cryptographic specifics.

Attachments included in the drive bundle: redwood_kms_key_lifecycle_attestation.pdf (attestation stub), dataflow_diagram_redwood_inference_v3.png, subprocessor_contract_addendum_v3.docx.

If you want a single PDF evidence pack we can package these along with a one-page summary that cites relevant DPA sections and clauses. Marissa — can you prepare the procurement-facing summary and the DocuSign envelope if Medico confirms?

Thanks,
